const patch = "*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /tmp/donor-resolve-design-luna.md
+# Individual donor name resolution sketch
+
+## Grounded path
+
+`clean` serializes the parallel name features in `FunderNameFeatures` to `cleaned/declarations/funders.parquet`. That table already includes `person_name_normalized`, which is title-free and also unwraps a parenthesized given name such as `(Michael) Farmer`. `resolve` deserializes rows into `declaration_resolution::Observation`, which currently drops that column. `ResolutionInput::scoring_input` groups identical raw-normalized name/address profiles, creates candidate blocking keys, and sends `ComparisonRow`s to the configured scorer. `identity::classify` then decides whether a scored observation pair can link. Its `kind()` already classifies Individual/Person, organisation, and unknown evidence; `company()` protects company identifiers.
+
+The missing link is therefore a consumer for the existing parsed person feature across deserialization, candidate blocking, and pair classification. The `person_name_normalized` field is an identity candidate, not source evidence or an unconditional identity assertion.
+
+## Contract
+
+Usage after implementation:
+
+```text
+clean source declarations -> preserve raw names and person_name_normalized
+resolve -> score candidate pairs -> link matching title-free keys only when both
+observations are donor-role and kind() says Person
+```
+
+The producer remains the only parser of titles and parenthetical given names. The existing `identity::kind()` remains the only person/organisation/unknown classifier. Add no second list of kind strings. Raw `name_raw`, `name_normalized`, and all cleaned evidence remain intact and scorer-facing `ComparisonRow.name` remains the ordinary normalized source name.
+
+## Minimal shape
+
+1. Add `person_name_normalized: Option<String>` to `Observation` and deserialize the existing cleaned parquet column. Validate that a present value is non-empty, like other normalized fields. Keep absent values valid for compatibility with hand-built test observations if the current artifact-version contract permits them; otherwise reject old artifacts through the existing schema/version error path.
+2. In `scoring_input`, add a `person-name:<key>` blocking key only when `observation.role == Donor`, `identity::kind(observation) == Person`, and the parsed key is present. Keep current name and alias keys. This reaches distinct title/plain/parenthesized profiles without broadening candidates for organisations, unknown kinds, or payer roles. Candidate generation already consumes shared blocking keys and honors the configured budget.
+3. In `identity::classify`, after rejecting a known person/organisation conflict and before the current exact-name donor shortcut, accept equal non-empty `person_name_normalized` values only when both roles are Donor and both existing `kind()` results are Person. Record a distinct pair reason/basis for this evidence if the current output vocabulary needs to distinguish it from exact raw-name linking. Do not lower thresholds or let the statistical score alone trigger this deterministic rule.
+4. Keep payer and ultimate-payer observations out of this rule. Keep company-number identity, organisation alias logic, exact raw donor-name behavior, unresolved-kind handling, and all raw evidence behavior as-is.
+
+## Identity rule and safety
+
+```text
+same_individual_name(a, b) =
+  a.role == Donor && b.role == Donor
+  && kind(a) == Person && kind(b) == Person
+  && a.person_name_normalized.is_some()
+  && a.person_name_normalized == b.person_name_normalized
+```
+
+This intentionally handles known `Individual`/`Person` donors only. It will not merge a person with an unclassified observation, even if their strings normalize alike. It may merge two distinct people who share the exact parsed full name; that's the same collision risk as the existing exact donor-name link, but restricting it to explicit person kinds avoids extending that risk to organisation and unknown records. Missing or malformed parsed keys never merge. Parenthesized titles or role annotations are not used as identity evidence unless the existing parser emits the same title-free person key.
+
+## Name-key choice
+
+Consume the existing title-free `person_name_normalized`, rather than retaining titles or deriving a new key in resolution. Titles vary across records for one person and should not block candidate discovery. The parser already recognizes and strips honorifics and unwraps `(Given) Surname`, so re-parsing raw names would duplicate parser ownership and risk divergence. Keep the original normalized name as the scorer's name feature so its statistical model still sees the source spelling differences; use the title-free value only as a blocking key and a narrowly gated deterministic equality rule.
+
+## Regression
+
+Extend `declaration_resolution_cli.rs`'s existing real `clean -> resolve` native-Weldrs regression with records for `Lord Michael Farmer`, `Michael Farmer`, `(Michael) Farmer`, and the corresponding Lord/plain/parenthesized `David Sainsbury` variants. Mark all as `Individual`. Assert each person's forms share one resolved identity, and the Farmer and Sainsbury identities differ. Assert observations and raw names remain present and distinct. Keep existing organisation, missing-kind, and payer coverage, or add explicit no-merge fixtures if not already covered by adjacent integration tests.
+
+The test must use the real scorer and assert resolved outputs, not private helper equality. Before the consumer exists, the title-free candidate blocking keys are absent and cross-profile variants cannot be joined by the intended deterministic rule, so this regression should fail; after implementation, it should pass. Candidate-budget behavior stays covered by the existing resolve CLI refusal assertion.
+
+## Alternative rejected
+
+Keeping titles in the key would miss the requested equivalence. Adding another title stripper or a donor-kind string allowlist in resolution would duplicate rules already owned by cleaning and `kind()`. Replacing scorer names with title-free names would throw away useful raw spelling evidence and alter scorer behavior beyond this task.
+
+## Scope
+
+Only thread one existing cleaned field into resolution, expose/reuse the existing entity classification within the resolution module, and add one person-only blocking key plus one gated pair rule and CLI regression. No production donor names or donor-specific exceptions belong in code.
*** End Patch";
text(await tools.apply_patch(patch));
